idiom_name: Iterator[A] with abstract hasNext/next, one-shot cursor
implementation_notes: Scala's standard library ships the pattern directly: scala.collection.Iterator[A] is a one-shot cursor whose abstract members are hasNext and next (nextOption and friends are conveniences), IterableOnce/Iterable are the aggregates, and for-comprehensions desugar to foreach/map/flatMap calls, so the traversal protocol is the collection API itself. The documented contract is stricter than in most languages: apart from next/hasNext, calling any method on an iterator may consume it ('one should never use an iterator after calling a method on it'), and a result is reusable only when the operation returned a strict collection. Use an Iterator for effectful or unbounded sources (files, DB cursors, generated data) and a strict collection or View when the result must be traversed twice.
code_sketch:
val it: Iterator[Order] = orders.iterator.filter(_.isPending)
while (it.hasNext) ship(it.next())                 // explicit cursor
for (o <- orders.iterator if o.isPending) ship(o)  // desugars to foreach
pitfalls: Iterator methods consume the iterator: calling size/length or any derived operation before the real traversal silently drains it, which is the documented 'never use an iterator after calling a method' rule.
hasNext may itself perform work (blocking IO, prefetching) when the source is IO-backed, so a 'check then next' loop can change timing or cost.
Iterator is mutable and not thread-safe: sharing one across threads or futures interleaves next/hasNext and loses elements.

variants.name: Lazy Views over strict collections
variants.idiom_name: collection.view with lazy map/filter/take, forced by a terminal conversion
variants.implementation_notes: The Scala 2.13 collections rework makes laziness a first-class alternative: .view turns a strict collection into a lazy View whose operations are applied on demand, and forcing it back (.toList/.to(Vector)) separates the traversal description from the materialized result. Unlike Iterator a View is reusable - forcing it again re-runs the transformation over the immutable source - so it fits chainable, repeatable pipelines; LazyList (2.13, formerly Stream) goes further and memoizes a lazy, possibly infinite sequence. Choose views for transformation chains over immutable data and iterators for effectful one-shot sources.
variants.code_sketch:
val report = orders.view.filter(_.isPending).map(_.amount).take(4)
report.foreach(println)   // runs the pipeline
report.toList             // reusable: re-runs the transformations
pitfalls: A view re-evaluates on every forced traversal, so side-effecting lambdas inside one run many times - acceptable only because the underlying collection is immutable.
Mixing views with iterators blurs when work happens: every toIterator/toList is a materialization point, and a view over a mutable source observes changes made after it was created.
LazyList memoizes consumed elements, so retaining the head of a long lazy sequence keeps the whole prefix alive (a space leak), the classic lazy-collection trap.
